procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
Tim Rush (coach of GBR 55244) attended the hearing as observer.
FRA 57041 was represented by Jeanne Amirault.
GBR 55244 was represented by Hector Davies.
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident in race 4 of the 420 U17 white fleet were 17 knots of wind and 1,5 meters waves.
In the pre-start area, FRA 57041 was on starboard tack and GBR 55244 was on port tack 10 boat lengths behind the starting line, 10 minutes before the start, on converging courses.
Both boats were not aware of their surroundings and all the crews were watching the start of the green fleet.
Contact occurred between GBR 55244’s bow and the port side, below the trapeze of FRA 57041 causing an L-shaped crack of 15cmx20cm in the hull of FRA 57401.
FRA 57041 returned to shore because she was taking in water and did not sail in race 4.
conclusions: GBR 55244 on port tack failed to keep clear of FRA 57041 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
GBR 55244 did not avoid contact with FRA 57041 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).

When it became clear that GBR 55244 was not keeping clear it was reasonably possible for FRA 57041, the right-of-way boat, to avoid contact with GBR 55244. FRA 57041 broke RRS 14(a). 4. Since FRA 57041 incurred serious damage by her breach, her penalty was to retire as required by RRS 44.1(b).
FRA 57041’s score in race 4 was made significantly worse through her own fault. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 64.1(b) are not met.
decision: Since FRA 57041 took an applicable penalty, she is not further penalized under RRS 60.5(c)(2).
Redress is not given to FRA 57041.
